status: subjective hypothesis-based expert assessment, NOT an empirical benchmark
scoring_method: 0-5 ordinal values with permitted 0.5 and tenths; weighted score = SUM(criteria.weight * option.score) / 100, maximum 5. Scores reflect CURRENT code reuse and FUTURE architecture fit, NOT measured runtime speed or precise cost.

criteria.name: Dense tables, keyboard interaction and data-grid ergonomics
Charting, scientific plots, zoom/pan and visualization flexibility
Direct use of existing JS Python and Sheets workspaces
Preserving existing Dart domain behavior, migration and delivery risk
Browser-native navigation, accessibility and UI integration
Static-first hosting simplicity and infrastructure fit
Potential for performance tuning (not measured performance)
Public pages, static generation and SEO options

options.name: React + TypeScript + Vite, client-side routed SPA
options.rationale: Best direct fit for a static-first browser workbench and existing JS Labs, but large Dart UI/rule port, data schema work, limited SEO without pre-rendering.

options.name: React + TypeScript + Next.js App Router
options.rationale: React tools and server-rendered public routes, with additional framework/runtime/static-export constraints for browser-only IDE and Sheets.

options.name: Retain Flutter shell and Dart analytics with browser-native feature modules
options.rationale: Fastest low-risk evolutionary path without a full rewrite; adds iframe/DOM integration, two UI rendering systems, accessibility and keyboard ownership complexity.

options.name: Vue 3 + Nuxt
options.rationale: Credible web-native alternative with hybrid rendering but no Arcside-specific gain over React to offset porting costs.

options.name: Svelte + SvelteKit
options.rationale: Credible lean UI framework; Arcside's current Monaco/JS assets integrate, but smaller matched tooling/integration evidence.

options.name: Keep Flutter and modularly refactor screens
options.rationale: Best preservation and native reuse, capable custom chart painter, but browser-native grids/Labs shell integration and DOM semantics need extra work.

uncertainty: A difference of 0.145/5 between first and third candidates is too small to justify a rewrite without matched proof of concept. React+Vite wins baseline assumptions; Flutter hybrid wins short-horizon delivery; Next.js wins SEO-first; Flutter wins native mobile first.
decision: Conditional preference: React+Vite for long-term browser-first workbench, Flutter+web hybrid as near-term fallback; no migration authorized until Phase 3 empirical gates pass.
data_quality: no controlled browser benchmark or engineering work-hour measurement available
